1	# SMA-860: capture a zero-argument tool-call stream for five conformance subjects
2	
3	- **Linear:** SMA-860 (follow-up of SMA-567)
4	- **Date:** 2026-11-24
5	- **Branch:** `feature/sma-860-capture-a-zero-argument-tool-call-stream-for`
6	
7	## 1. Intent
8	
9	SMA-567 added the `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` scenario to the stream conformance suite
10	(`tests/provider-stream-conformance`). Only `openai/responses` serves it. Five subjects are pinned
11	in the `UNCAPTURED` table with SMA-860 as the follow-up: `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `gemini`,
12	`litellm` and `openai/chat`.
13	
14	The suite accepts a fixture only if it meets the provenance rule (`CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format
15	fixtures"). So each of the five subjects needs a real capture before it can serve the scenario.
16	This change adds the five captures, serves the scenario from them, and removes the five rows.
17	
18	## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals
19	
20	**Goals.**
21	
22	- G1. Each of the five subjects serves `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` from a committed CAPTURED fixture.
23	- G2. Each fixture has a provenance header that lists every edit from the raw capture.
24	- G3. The five `UNCAPTURED` rows for `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` are removed.
25	- G4. The design records what each provider actually sends for a zero-argument call. The ticket
26	  asks for this, in particular for a stream with no argument deltas and for the Gemini `null`
27	  arguments.
28	
29	**Non-goals.**
30	
31	- No change to a provider translator, unless the suite finds a conformance failure (SMA-533
32	  design §9 applies). §5 predicts that no failure occurs.
33	- No change to the `ReasoningCleanStop` rows (SMA-858) or the `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` rows
34	  (SMA-859).
35	- No new scenario. A stream with truly zero argument deltas has no capture (§4), so this change
36	  adds no scenario for it.
37	
38	**Anti-goals.**
39	
40	- A fixture that is labelled CAPTURED but has an edit that its header does not record.
41	- A script that "fixes" a capture so that it matches a sibling subject.
42	
43	## 3. Approach
44	
45	Three approaches were considered:
46	
47	- **A. Commit a fixture file and copy its payloads into `conformance.rs`.** This is the
48	  `ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` pattern of the `openai/responses` subject (SMA-567). The SMA-567 design (§6.9)
49	  requires it. The risk is drift between the copy and the file. Only review prevents it.
50	- **B. Commit a fixture file and `include_str!` it from the script.** No drift can occur. But this
51	  adds a new pattern and a frame parser for each wire format.
52	- **C. Record the capture only in the module doc** (the Gemini "Live capture" pattern). This is the
53	  weakest provenance, because doc comments usually elide values.
54	
55	**Sven picked A** on 2026-11-24.
56	
57	## 4. The captures
58	
59	Claude ran all five captures on 2026-11-24 with Sven's keys, at Sven's request. Each request
60	offered one tool, `get_current_time`, with the description "Return the current server time. Takes
61	no arguments." and the user message "What time is it?". Each request forced the tool call. The
62	exact request bodies are committed in `docs/superpowers/specs/sma-860-requests/`. Request headers
63	(keys) are not recorded.
64	
65	| Subject | Endpoint | Model | Time (UTC) | Argument deltas on the wire |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | 20:38:59 | One `input_json_delta` with `partial_json: ""`. `content_block_start` carries `"input":{}`. |
68	| `openai/chat` | `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` | `gpt-5-mini` (reported `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07`) | 20:39:21 | The first `tool_calls` delta has `arguments: ""`. One more delta has `arguments: "{}"`. |
69	| `gemini` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | 20:39:23 | No deltas. One `functionCall` part with `"args": {}`. |
70	| `bedrock` | `https://bedrock-runtime.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/model/eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5/converse-stream` | `eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` (inference profile) | 20:39:45 | One `contentBlockDelta` with `toolUse.input: ""`. |
71	| `litellm` | LiteLLM 1.98.0 proxy (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm@sha256:3a1980074ff2ac13883e0ffee1bebec345d8addd004be251079cee173b0e8305`), `/v1/chat/completions`, upstream `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | 20:59:06 | Three `tool_calls` deltas: `""`, `""`, `"{}"`. |
72	
73	Raw sizes and SHA-256 of the bytes as received:
74	
75	| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| anthropic | 1364 | `b6114d956d7d80a6b315fcd2f6866fff8c776e9ebbed846c8ab7ccf9093dd86e` |
78	| openai/chat | 1618 | `5c5e74ac372aa0f954e89801c0addb62592a1ae02ad3c36b427b4d24f56d8cf2` |
79	| gemini | 1327 | `2bda3e52f91da7cbe66dac254ae8865fbd64f22a8ade1a3a7c5cf206cd2a8305` |
80	| bedrock (binary) | 1250 | `9196618e83783e261b5a3997d81a8cb343ff58bb1c560bff611a53c0d6a98b04` |
81	| litellm | 1739 | `b81bc790cdcf6a93e1ef6e8391a353a344d95549ef08a412ee0f7c1f241552c7` |
82	
83	**Findings.**
84	
85	1. **No provider sent a stream with truly zero argument deltas.** Anthropic and Bedrock send one
86	   delta with an empty string. So the accumulated arguments text is `""`, not `{}`. Gemini sends
87	   the whole call in one part. A zero-delta stream still has no capture for any subject.
88	2. **Gemini sent `"args": {}`, not a missing `args`.** The `"null"` path in
89	   `providers-gemini/src/sse.rs` did not occur in this capture. The request declared the tool with
90	   no `parameters` field at all. The capture does not show what Gemini sends for a declaration with
91	   an empty `properties` object. This change does not test that.
92	3. **LiteLLM changes the Anthropic shape.** Upstream Anthropic sends `""` (finding 1). LiteLLM
93	   emits `""`, `""` and then `"{}"`. So LiteLLM adds a `{}` that the upstream did not send.
94	4. Each capture has fields that the translators do not know, for example `caller` (Anthropic,
95	   LiteLLM), `p` padding (Bedrock), `obfuscation` (OpenAI) and `inference_geo`. The scripts keep
96	   them, because a CAPTURED payload is sent byte for byte.
97	
98	## 5. Expected suite behaviour
99	
100	The `ToolCallsMismatch` floor (`lib.rs`, near line 1032) and assertion 10 (`check.rs`, near line
101	192) both read blank arguments as `{}`. So the `""` arguments of `anthropic` and `bedrock` match
102	the declared call `get_current_time` with `{}`. No translator change is expected. If a subject
103	fails, the builder stops, records the failure, and treats it as a SMA-533 §9 finding. The builder
104	does not edit the capture to make it pass.
105	
106	## 6. Design
107	
108	### 6.1 Fixture files
109	
110	One committed file for each subject. The raw bytes are already in the worktree at these paths
111	(untracked). The builder adds the header and leaves the payload lines unchanged.
112	
113	| Subject | Path |
114	|---|---|
115	| `anthropic` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/tool_use_zero_args.txt` |
116	| `openai/chat` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_tool_call_zero_args.txt` |
117	| `gemini` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/fixtures/tool_call_zero_args.sse` |
118	| `litellm` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/tool_call_stream_zero_args.txt` |
119	| `bedrock` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/tests/fixtures/converse_stream_tool_use_zero_args.bin` (raw) and `converse_stream_tool_use_zero_args.txt` (decoded) |
120	
121	Header rules (from `CONTRIBUTING.md`, rules 1, 2 and 5):
122	
123	- Label CAPTURED. Name the endpoint, the model, the date and time, the request body file in
124	  `docs/superpowers/specs/sma-860-requests/`, and SMA-860.
125	- List Removed, Added and Changed. For the four text files the only edit is the header itself:
126	  Removed nothing, Added the `:` header lines, Changed nothing. Real ids, signatures and padding
127	  are kept verbatim. Gemini's `thoughtSignature` is kept, unlike `parallel_signed.sse`, so that no
128	  value edit exists.
129	- Give the raw byte count and SHA-256 from §4, so that a reader can check the payload lines.
130	- Bedrock: the `.bin` file is the raw capture, with no header (it has no comment syntax). The
131	  `.txt` file is a decoded view of it, with a `:` header. Each frame becomes one `event:` line (the
132	  `:event-type` header value) and one `data:` line (the payload bytes, verbatim). The header
133	  records the decode under Changed: the prelude, header encoding and CRCs are dropped, and the
134	  `:content-type` (`application/json`) and `:message-type` (`event`) headers are dropped because
135	  they are the same on all six frames. The builder writes the decode with a small throwaway
136	  script and checks that the six payloads match the `.bin` file.
137	- The header says what §4 found for this subject (the argument deltas).
138	
139	Add `*.bin binary` for the new Bedrock fixture directory to `.gitattributes`, so that git never
140	changes its bytes. (Builder's call: the existing LF rule covers only the anthropic `*.txt` files.
141	The scripts copy the payloads into consts, so line endings of the other text fixtures do not affect
142	a test.)
143	
144	### 6.2 Scripts
145	
146	In each of the five subject modules in `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs`:
147	
148	- Replace the `Outcome::Uncaptured(..)` return for `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` with a served
149	  script.
150	- Copy the capture payloads into a const, named the same as in `openai_responses`
151	  (`ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` or `ZERO_ARG_CHUNKS`, whichever matches the subject's framing). Each payload
152	  is the exact `data:` text of the fixture. Anthropic and LiteLLM payloads keep their trailing
153	  spaces inside the line.
154	- Send every frame of the capture, in order, including the Anthropic `ping` event and the
155	  `data: [DONE]` sentinel of `openai/chat` and `litellm`. Gemini ends at bare EOF, as captured;
156	  do not add the synthetic `done()`.
157	- Bedrock: encode each (event type, payload) pair with the suite's `eventstream.rs` encoder.
158	- Write the arm comment in the form of the `openai_responses` arm: the source file, the capture,
159	  and "Edits made here", which must be only framing.
160	- `request()` offers `get_current_time` for this scenario. `fixture_calls()` returns
161	  `get_current_time` with `{}`.
162	
163	### 6.3 Tables
164	
165	- Remove the five `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` rows from `UNCAPTURED` in `src/declines.rs`.
166	- Remove `Scenario::ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` from `UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS`. No row names it any
167	  more, and a future row must again need a reviewed edit.
168	- Update the comment above the removed rows and any doc that says only `openai/responses` serves
169	  the scenario (the builder searches for `SMA-860` and "only `openai/responses`").
170	
171	### 6.4 Documentation
172	
173	- No mdBook or README change. This is a change to an unpublished test crate and to test fixtures.
174	  It changes no public API.
175	- Fixture files under `crates/*/tests/` are in the published packages (no crate sets `include` or
176	  `exclude`). So release-plz will give the five provider crates a patch bump and the facade a
177	  cascade. This is expected and harmless.
178	
179	### 6.5 Verification
180	
181	- `cargo test -p provider-stream-conformance` (use the package name from its `Cargo.toml`) passes.
182	- A negative check for each subject: change the copied arguments of the zero-argument call to
183	  `{"x":1}` and confirm the suite fails with `ToolCallsMismatch`. Then revert.
184	- The full CI gate list in `CLAUDE.md`.
185	
186	## 7. Left to the builder
187	
188	- Const names and helper functions for framing, if they follow the existing subject module.
189	- The exact header wording, inside the rules in §6.1.
190	- Whether the Bedrock decode script is kept. It is not committed, unless it is needed to verify.

211	/// the table would otherwise be silently invisible: `pinned_problems`
212	/// only ever runs with a real subject's name, filtering [`DECLINED`] down to
213	/// the rows for that one subject. A row naming a subject that does not exist
214	/// never matches that filter for *any* real subject, so it is never checked
215	/// in either direction — not flagged as an unexpected decline, and not
216	/// flagged as a pinned decline that stopped happening. The reverse direction
217	/// (a real subject declining something absent from the table) does fail
218	/// loudly; this is the direction that previously did not.

310	                 UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS"

312	        }

200	## Wire-format fixtures
201	
202	A wire-format fixture is a file or test script that stands in for the bytes a provider sends. A reader must know which bytes are real and which bytes are not. Five rules apply.
203	
204	SMA-585 shows the risk. `responses_tool_call.txt` is a CAPTURED fixture, but the file ended with a `[DONE]` line that the Responses endpoint does not send. The header did not record the line.
205	
206	1. **Label.** Each fixture states its provenance. Use one of three labels: CAPTURED (name the endpoint, the model and the date), HAND-AUTHORED, or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts.
207	2. **Edits.** A CAPTURED fixture lists every edit from the raw capture in three parts: Removed, Added and Changed. Changed covers reorders, reformats and value edits. Write "nothing" only when the record shows that a part is empty. If the raw capture is not available, write "not recorded" for a part that you cannot check, and say what evidence exists. The header of `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt` is the worked example.
208	3. **Hand-authored shapes.** A HAND-AUTHORED fixture names the source of each shape. The source is a capture or a vendored type. Do not copy framing from a different endpoint or API.
209	4. **No conformity edits.** Do not add, remove or reorder a line to make a fixture match a sibling fixture. If you must, record the edit under Changed.
210	5. **Where the header goes.** An SSE fixture or other text fixture carries a `:` comment header. A format with no comment syntax records its provenance in the doc comment of the test that loads it. An inline wire helper in test code cites its source in the same way. 1	//! The registered conformance subjects.
2	//!
3	//! Each subject in this file serves its own wire bytes through the crate's
4	//! paced HTTP server and hands back the stream from its real `Model::invoke`,
5	//! so every assertion in `assert_conforms` is made about production driver and
6	//! production translator code — never about a reimplementation of either.
7	//!
8	//! ## Adding a subject
9	//!
10	//! One `mod <subject> { … }` per subject, holding its fixture helpers, its
11	//! `StreamUnderTest` impl and one `#[tokio::test]` that calls
12	//! `assert_conforms`. The module scoping is not cosmetic: it is what lets every
13	//! subject call its helpers `text_delta`, `script`, `request` and so on without
14	//! a per-subject prefix, and it keeps six subjects' worth of near-identical
15	//! names from colliding in one flat namespace.
16	//!
17	//! Two rules apply to every subject, and both exist because breaking them makes
18	//! a check pass without measuring anything:
19	//!
20	//! 1. **Decline and uncaptured reasons are literal strings**, copied by hand
21	//!    from `src/declines.rs`. A subject that looked its reasons up from
22	//!    `DECLINED` or `UNCAPTURED` would satisfy that table's two-directional
23	//!    cross-check by construction, which is exactly the drift the table exists
24	//!    to catch.
25	//! 2. **`encodes_stop_reason` is measured from the bytes about to be served**,
26	//!    never restated from `Scenario::expects_stop_reason`. Restating it
27	//!    compares the harness's expectation with itself. See the Bedrock impl for
28	//!    what it catches.
29	//!
30	//! ## Key order
31	//!
32	//! Each wire helper that builds a JSON payload uses `json!` and serializes the
33	//! `serde_json::Value`. (The `done()` helpers are byte literals.) The
34	//! `serde_json` 1.0.154 in `Cargo.lock` has no `preserve_order` feature, so
35	//! the keys come out in alphabetical order. That order can differ from the
36	//! order in the cited sources. No translator depends on key order: each one
37	//! decodes the payload as a JSON object.
38	
39	use paigasus_helikon_core::{
40	    CancellationToken, ContentPart, FinishReason, Item, Model, ModelRequest, ToolDef,
41	};
42	use paigasus_helikon_provider_stream_conformance::{
43	    assert_conforms, eventstream::frame, Channel, Ending, ExpectedCall, Outcome, PacedServer,
44	    Scenario, Script, StreamUnderTest,
45	};
46	use serde_json::json;
47	
48	/// The `Model::invoke` stream contract, checked against the Bedrock
49	/// `ConverseStream` provider.
50	///
51	/// # Fixture provenance
52	///
53	/// Label: HAND-AUTHORED, from the vendored `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime` types and
54	/// the translator's match arms. No helper here is a capture.
55	///
56	/// Bedrock is the one subject in this suite whose wire format is binary, and
57	/// the repo holds no captured Bedrock traffic to transcribe. So — as the task
58	/// brief directs when no capture exists — every event shape here is derived
59	/// from two sources inside the workspace, and from nothing else:
60	///
61	/// 1. **The translator's own match arms**, `providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`.

63	///    carry to produce a `ModelEvent`, is read off the arms that consume them:
64	///    `ContentBlockDelta`/`Text` to `TokenDelta`, `ContentBlockStart`/`ToolUse`

69	///    every `:event-type` is the union member name its
70	///    `ConverseStreamOutputUnmarshaller` dispatches on
71	///    (`src/event_stream_serde.rs`). Per-shape references sit on each helper.

74	/// from those two sources: a frame the SDK's decoder does not recognise is
75	/// dropped silently by the translator's forward-compat catch-all rather than
76	/// rejected, so a shape from outside them would present as a translator bug

219	    /// The scripted response for one scenario, or `None` for a scenario this
220	    /// subject declines or has no capture for (an uncaptured scenario).
221	    ///
222	    /// Each script is the same Converse stream cut at a different point, so the
223	    /// scenarios differ only in what the client gets to observe — which is
224	    /// exactly the distinction the suite is checking.
225	    ///
226	    /// Returning an `Option` rather than panicking on the declined or uncaptured
227	    /// scenarios is what lets [`Bedrock::encodes_stop_reason`] call this for *every*
228	    /// scenario and measure the bytes.
229	    fn script(scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Script> {
230	        // The prefix every text script shares: the opening event and two
231	        // deltas, so a cancellation can be gated *between* two `TokenDelta`s
232	        // rather than before the first one.
233	        let opening = || vec![message_start(), text_delta("Hel"), text_delta("lo")];
234	        // The opening plus a completed block and a stop reason.
235	        let through_stop = || {
236	            let mut chunks = opening();
237	            chunks.push(content_block_stop());
238	            chunks.push(message_stop("end_turn"));
239	            chunks
240	        };
241	
242	        let (chunks, gate_after, ending) = match scenario {
243	            // Full stream: deltas, stop reason, then the usage-bearing metadata
244	            // event after it, then a clean end of body.
245	            Scenario::CleanStop => {
246	                let mut chunks = through_stop();
247	                chunks.push(metadata());
248	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
249	            }
250	            // The stop reason is observed, then the body simply ends — no
251	            // `metadata`, so the translator's buffered stop reason has to be
252	            // flushed by the EOF path in `model.rs` (`translator.finish()`).
253	            Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Clean),
254	            // The body ends cleanly mid-generation: no `messageStop`, so no
255	            // stop reason is ever observed and there is nothing to flush.
256	            Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Clean),
257	            // Same prefix, but the connection is torn down without the
258	            // terminating chunk, so the SDK's receiver yields a transport error.
259	            Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Abort),
260	            // The stop reason is buffered and *then* the body is aborted, so
261	            // the error path must not flush it as a `Finish`.
262	            Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Abort),
263	            // Two chunks go out — `messageStart` and the first delta — and the
264	            // server then parks, holding the second delta back. The harness
265	            // sees the stream fall quiet and cancels. No `messageStop` anywhere
266	            // in this script, so no stop reason exists even after the gate is
267	            // released.
268	            Scenario::CancelMidGeneration => (opening(), Some(2), Ending::Clean),
269	            // A whole tool call: the name arrives with the block start, the
270	            // arguments arrive split across two deltas (so exactly one emitted
271	            // `ToolCallDelta` carries the name), then a `tool_use` stop reason
272	            // and the usage-bearing metadata event.
273	            Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop => (
274	                vec![
275	                    message_start(),
276	                    tool_use_start(),
277	                    tool_use_delta("{\"city\":"),
278	                    tool_use_delta("\"Berlin\"}"),
279	                    content_block_stop(),
280	                    message_stop("tool_use"),
281	                    metadata(),
282	                ],
283	                None,
284	                Ending::Clean,
285	            ),
286	            // Declined — see the reasons in `Bedrock::stream`.
287	            Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason | Scenario::FragmentedToolName => return None,
288	            // Declined — the scenario serves an anthropic thinking block.
289	            Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => return None,
290	            // Not served — see the reason in `stream`.
291	            Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop => return None,
292	            // Not served — see the reason in `stream`.
293	            Scenario::ParallelToolCallCleanStop => return None,
294	            // Not served — see the reason in `stream`.
295	            Scenario::ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop => return None,
296	        };
297	
298	        Some(Script {
299	            content_type: "application/vnd.amazon.eventstream",
300	            chunks,
301	            gate_after,
302	            ending,
303	        })
304	    }

390	        fn encodes_stop_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> bool {
391	            // MEASURED from the bytes about to be served — deliberately not
392	            // `scenario.expects_stop_reason()`, which would restate the
393	            // harness's own expectation and make the cross-check dead code.
394	            //
395	            // It has to measure something, because one scenario is otherwise
396	            // undetectable if its fixture drifts: `ErrorAfterStopReason`'s
397	            // observable events are `[TokenDelta, TokenDelta, Err]`, byte-for-
398	            // byte identical to `ErrorMidGeneration`'s. If `through_stop()`
399	            // ever lost its `messageStop`, that scenario would silently degrade
400	            // into its sibling with every check in the suite still passing —
401	            // assertion 3 skips itself when an `Err` is present, and assertion 6
402	            // holds either way. This is the only guard that notices.
403	            //
404	            // A substring scan is sound here. In a `vnd.amazon.eventstream`
405	            // frame the `:event-type` header value is stored as raw ASCII, so
406	            // `"messageStop"` appears literally in any frame that carries it.
407	            // It cannot appear anywhere else in these fixtures: no other event
408	            // name this subject emits contains it (`messageStart` and
409	            // `contentBlockStop` are the near misses, and neither does), and no
410	            // payload above contains the text. `scan_finds_only_the_stop_event`
411	            // is the test that keeps that true.
412	            script(scenario)
413	                .map(|script| {
414	                    script
415	                        .chunks
416	                        .iter()
417	                        .any(|chunk| contains(chunk, MESSAGE_STOP_EVENT_TYPE.as_bytes()))
418	                })
419	                .unwrap_or(false)
420	        }

531	        use aws_smithy_eventstream::frame::{DecodedFrame, MessageFrameDecoder};
532	
533	        chunks
534	            .iter()
535	            .map(|chunk| {
536	                let mut decoder = MessageFrameDecoder::new();
537	                let message = match decoder
538	                    .decode_frame(chunk.as_slice())
539	                    .expect("a frame this module wrote must decode")
540	                {
541	                    DecodedFrame::Complete(message) => message,
542	                    DecodedFrame::Incomplete => panic!("each chunk must be one complete frame"),
543	                };
544	                message
545	                    .headers()
546	                    .iter()
547	                    .find(|h| h.name().as_str() == ":event-type")
548	                    .expect("every frame carries an :event-type header")
549	                    .value()
550	                    .as_string()
551	                    .expect(":event-type is a string header")
552	                    .as_str()
553	                    .to_owned()
554	            })
555	            .collect()
556	    }

560	    /// Bedrock sends `messageStop` first. `stream.rs` accepts both orders, so

1	//! Hand-built `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` frames, so a Bedrock
2	//! fixture can be written as JSON instead of as opaque captured bytes.
3	//!
4	//! Bedrock is the only subject in this suite whose wire format is binary. Every
5	//! other provider streams SSE, which a fixture file can hold verbatim; an
6	//! eventstream frame carries two CRC-32s over a length-prefixed header block,
7	//! so a hand-typed `.bin` fixture is neither reviewable nor editable. Building
8	//! the frames with the same encoder the SDK itself uses keeps the fixture
9	//! readable *and* keeps the bytes on the wire real: `Model::invoke` runs its
10	//! production transport, the SDK's own decoder parses these frames, and the
11	//! production translator sees genuine `ConverseStreamOutput` values.
12	//!
13	//! ## The silent-drop hazard
14	//!
15	//! `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs` ends its `match`
16	//! with a forward-compat catch-all that ignores unknown
17	//! `ConverseStreamOutput` variants. A frame whose `:event-type` does not match
18	//! a union member name exactly therefore produces **no error and no event** —
19	//! it simply vanishes. The failure presents as an empty stream and reads like a
20	//! translator bug, so the header names below are load-bearing and are pinned by
21	//! `frame_headers_are_exactly_the_three_the_decoder_requires`.
22	
23	use aws_smithy_eventstream::frame::write_message_to;
24	use aws_smithy_types::event_stream::{Header, HeaderValue, Message};
25	
26	/// Encode one Bedrock `ConverseStream` event as a complete
27	/// `vnd.amazon.eventstream` frame.
28	///
29	/// `event_type` is the union member name **exactly** as the Bedrock model
30	/// spells it — `messageStart`, `contentBlockStart`, `contentBlockDelta`,
31	/// `contentBlockStop`, `messageStop`, `metadata`. `payload` is the event's JSON
32	/// body, serialised as the frame payload.
33	///
34	/// The returned bytes are a self-contained frame (prelude, headers, payload,
35	/// message CRC) and can be handed to the paced server as one chunk, or split
36	/// across chunks to exercise a decoder that has to reassemble them.
37	///
38	/// # Panics
39	///
40	/// Panics if `payload` cannot be serialised (only reachable for a
41	/// `serde_json::Value` containing a map with non-string keys, which the `json!`
42	/// macro cannot build) or if the encoder rejects the message.
43	pub fn frame(event_type: &str, payload: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
44	    let body = serde_json::to_vec(payload).expect("frame payload should serialise");
45	
46	    // All three headers are string headers, and all three are required: the
47	    // SDK's `parse_response_headers` errors without `:message-type`, dispatches
48	    // on `:event-type`, and the generated unmarshaller reads the payload as
49	    // JSON on the strength of `:content-type`.
50	    let message = Message::new_from_parts(
51	        vec![
52	            Header::new(":message-type", HeaderValue::String("event".into())),
53	            Header::new(
54	                ":event-type",
55	                // `StrBytes: From<&'static str>` only, so an ordinary `&str`
56	                // has to go through `String`.
57	                HeaderValue::String(event_type.to_owned().into()),
58	            ),
59	            Header::new(
60	                ":content-type",
61	                HeaderValue::String("application/json".into()),
62	            ),
63	        ],
64	        body,
65	    );
66	
67	    let mut buf = Vec::new();
68	    write_message_to(&message, &mut buf).expect("eventstream message should encode");
69	    buf
70	}

657	/// The `Model::invoke` stream contract, checked against the OpenAI Chat
658	/// Completions backend.
659	///
660	/// This is the subject whose historical defect motivated the whole suite:
661	/// SMA-522 (PR #197), where this exact translator emitted `Finish` before
662	/// `Usage` on every streaming turn. It went undetected because the fixtures
663	/// in place at the time put `usage` *before* `finish_reason`. The SMA-522
664	/// LiteLLM proxy capture (`chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`) shows `usage`
665	/// after `finish_reason`. `CleanStop` below places `usage` after the
666	/// `finish_reason` chunk for exactly that reason.
667	///
668	/// # Fixture provenance
669	///
670	/// Every envelope shape below is transcribed from a committed fixture in this
671	/// workspace, cited on the helper that builds it. Each source is either a
672	/// capture through a LiteLLM proxy or a hand-authored file. No capture of
673	/// `api.openai.com` Chat Completions is recorded in the repo.
674	///
675	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`
676	///   — CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts, through a LiteLLM proxy with
677	///   a keyless `mock_response` (SMA-522, PR #197): content deltas, the
678	///   `finish_reason` chunk, the trailing `usage` chunk, `[DONE]`.
679	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/chat_wire.rs`'s
680	///   `happy_path_text_completion` fixture body — HAND-AUTHORED. It is the
681	///   source of the explicit `"finish_reason":null` that [`text_delta`] sends
682	///   on each content delta. No recorded capture sends that key on a content
683	///   delta: the LiteLLM captures omit it. The null is exactly the shape
684	///   [`OpenAiChat::encodes_stop_reason`]'s marker must not match.
685	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt`
686	///   — HAND-AUTHORED (SMA-316, PR #30). The tool-call envelope: `id`/`name`
687	///   arriving with empty `arguments`, followed by args-only continuations
688	///   with no `name` key.
689	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt`
690	///   — CAPTURED from LiteLLM 1.98.0 over a hand-written fake upstream
691	///   (SMA-547, PR #204). Only the LiteLLM serialization is captured; the ids,
692	///   the name split and the argument split are authored input. It holds a
693	///   name split across two deltas that BOTH arrive after the `id`. Per the
694	///   design spec's §6 provenance note, this is the capture
695	///   `FragmentedToolName`'s shape must be drawn from — the note requires the
696	///   committed **shape**, not byte-identical values; see
697	///   "`FragmentedToolName` deliberately never completes" below for exactly
698	///   what this module substitutes (the "id resolves late" variant has no
699	///   capture anywhere in the repo and is not built here).
700	///
701	/// `chat_content_filter.txt` and `chat_text_usage_trailing_empty_choices.txt`
702	/// (both HAND-AUTHORED) were read but contribute no shape this module needs:
703	/// this subject serves only `Stop` and `ToolCalls` finish reasons, and the
704	/// empty-`choices` usage variant is a second encoding of the same
705	/// trailing-usage envelope already covered by `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`.
706	///
707	/// # `FragmentedToolName` deliberately never completes
708	///
709	/// The task brief's scenario table describes `FragmentedToolName` as ending
710	/// with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` → `usage` → `[DONE]`, mirroring the
711	/// litellm capture's full trace. That shape was tried first and reverted: the
712	/// design spec's §6 table asserts only **7, 1** for this scenario (`S6`), not
713	/// 3/4, and `Scenario::expects_stop_reason` (`src/lib.rs`) excludes
714	/// `FragmentedToolName` from the set of scenarios that may observe a stop
715	/// reason. Completing the stream — which the real translator does, buffering
716	/// `finish_reason` and flushing it as a genuine `Finish` at end-of-stream —
717	/// makes `encodes_stop_reason` measure `true` against an `expects_stop_reason`
718	/// of `false`, failing on `StopReasonDeclarationMismatch` before the stream is
719	/// even drained. So this subject's `FragmentedToolName` script draws its
720	/// event sequence and key structure from that capture's first three frames —
721	/// not a byte-identical copy: `id`/`created`/`model` are this module's fixed
722	/// constants (`RESPONSE_ID`/`MODEL_ID`) rather than the capture's literal
723	/// values, `TOOL_CALL_ID` stands in for the capture's literal tool-call id,
724	/// and the first frame omits the capture's `"role":"assistant"` key
725	/// (`ChatTranslator` does not read it) — see the `FragmentedToolName` match
726	/// arm in `script`, below, for the exact substitutions. The body ends
727	/// cleanly right after those three frames — no `finish_reason`, no `usage`,
728	/// no `[DONE]`. Assertion 7 (exactly one name-bearing delta per `call_id`) is
729	/// fully exercised by that prefix alone; nothing here shortens what the
730	/// scenario tests, only when its script stops.
731	///
732	/// # SMA-566's alias regression coverage lives in the crate's own unit tests
733	///
734	/// Every tool-call delta this module scripts carries an explicit `"index":0`,
735	/// and no delta ever introduces a second `id` — the continuation frames
736	/// (`tool_call_name_fragment`, `tool_call_args`) omit the key entirely. Only
737	/// one index value is ever in play, so the two-index-one-id shape that
738	/// `ChatTranslator::canonicalize` exists to merge never arises from these
739	/// bytes, and assertion 7 passes here without exercising it. Under
740	/// this suite's fixture-provenance rule the shape has no capture anywhere in
741	/// the repo and must not be invented, so it is not registered as a scenario —
742	/// exactly as `litellm` records for its own `canonicalize`.
743	///
744	/// Read this subject's `conforms` test as confirming the translator behaves
745	/// correctly on the wire shapes this module scripts from the sources above,
746	/// **not** as a standing regression guard for the alias fix. That guard is
747	/// `two_indexes_with_one_id_merge_into_a_single_call` and its eleven siblings
748	/// in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs`. If a
749	/// future capture ever shows a backend reusing one `id` across two indexes,
750	/// that would be the fixture to add here; none currently committed does.
751	mod openai_chat {

756	    /// format — nothing under test inspects it — fixed purely so failure
757	    /// output is stable and greppable.
758	    const RESPONSE_ID: &str = "chatcmpl-conformance";

761	    /// requests. Matches the identifier the task brief specifies.

769	    const TOOL_CALL_ID: &str = "call_conformance_0";

771	    /// The substring that appears in a Chat Completions chunk if and only if
772	    /// that chunk carries a *populated* `finish_reason`.
773	    ///
774	    /// The obvious marker — `finish_reason` alone — is wrong for this
775	    /// subject: [`text_delta`] sends `"finish_reason":null` on every content
776	    /// delta (no recorded capture does; see its doc), so a bare substring
777	    /// scan would report a stop reason for scripts that encode none. Scanning
778	    /// for the opening quote of a *string* value excludes the null case:
779	    /// `null` has no quote after the colon, `"stop"`/`"tool_calls"` do.
780	    /// `scan_finds_only_a_populated_finish_reason` is the guard that keeps
781	    /// this true as helpers are added or edited.

784	    /// One SSE frame: `data: {payload}\n\n`. `serde_json::Value`'s `Display`

40	pub enum Scenario {
41	    /// Deltas, stop reason, usage, terminator, clean EOF.
42	    CleanStop,
43	    /// Stop reason observed, then the body ends cleanly with no terminator.
44	    TruncatedAfterStopReason,
45	    /// Body ends cleanly mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
46	    TruncatedMidGeneration,
47	    /// Body aborted mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
48	    ErrorMidGeneration,
49	    /// Stop reason observed, then the body is aborted.
50	    ErrorAfterStopReason,
51	    /// Cancelled mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
52	    CancelMidGeneration,
53	    /// Stop reason observed, then cancelled before end-of-stream.
54	    CancelAfterStopReason,
55	    /// A tool call whose name arrives split across two or more deltas.
56	    FragmentedToolName,
57	    /// One complete tool call followed by a tool-use stop reason.
58	    ToolCallCleanStop,
59	    /// A signed thinking block, then one complete tool call, then a tool-use
60	    /// stop reason.
61	    ThinkingToolCallCleanStop,
62	    /// Reasoning, then text, then one complete tool call, then a tool-use
63	    /// stop reason. Provider-neutral: any reasoning channel serves it.
64	    ReasoningCleanStop,
65	    /// Two or more complete tool calls, then a tool-use stop reason.
66	    ParallelToolCallCleanStop,
67	    /// One complete tool call with no arguments (a `{}` delta), then a
68	    /// tool-use stop reason.
69	    ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop,
70	}

72	impl Scenario {
73	    /// Every scenario, in table order.
74	    pub const ALL: &'static [Scenario] = &[
75	        Scenario::CleanStop,
76	        Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason,
77	        Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration,
78	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration,
79	        Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason,
80	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration,
81	        Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason,
82	        Scenario::FragmentedToolName,
83	        Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop,
84	        Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop,
85	        Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop,
86	        Scenario::ParallelToolCallCleanStop,
87	        Scenario::ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop,
88	    ];

90	    /// Whether this scenario's script must let the translator observe a stop
91	    /// reason. Cross-checked against each subject's own declaration so a
92	    /// mis-transcribed fixture cannot make assertion 3 pass vacuously.
93	    pub fn expects_stop_reason(self) -> bool {
94	        matches!(
95	            self,
96	            Scenario::CleanStop
97	                | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason
98	                | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
99	                | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
100	                | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
101	                | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
102	                | Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop
103	                | Scenario::ParallelToolCallCleanStop
104	                | Scenario::ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop
105	        )
106	    }
107	}
108	
109	/// One run of same-channel events, in wire order.
110	///
111	/// `ReasoningDelta`, `TokenDelta` and `ToolCallDelta` each map to one channel.
112	/// Adjacent events of one channel merge into one run.
113	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
114	pub enum Channel {
115	    /// `ReasoningDelta` events.
116	    Reasoning,
117	    /// `TokenDelta` events.
118	    Text,
119	    /// `ToolCallDelta` events.
120	    Tool,
121	}
122	
123	/// A tool call that a fixture carries: its name and its complete arguments as
124	/// JSON text.
125	///
126	/// `args` is text, not a parsed value, so that a table of calls can be a
127	/// `const`. The floor parses it.
128	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
129	pub struct ExpectedCall {
130	    /// The tool name of the call.
131	    pub name: &'static str,
132	    /// The complete arguments of the call, as JSON text.
133	    pub args: &'static str,
134	}
135	
136	/// A contract violation, classified. Ordering matters — see `classify`.
137	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
138	pub enum Violation {
139	    /// More than one `Finish` was emitted (assertion 1).
140	    DuplicateFinish,
141	    /// A `Usage` was emitted after `Finish` (assertion 2).
142	    UsageAfterFinish,
143	    /// Any other event, or an `Err`, was emitted after `Finish` (assertion 1).
144	    EventAfterFinish,
145	    /// End-of-stream after an observed stop reason emitted no `Finish`
146	    /// (assertion 3).
147	    MissingFinish,
148	    /// A `Finish` was emitted although no stop reason was observed
149	    /// (assertion 4).
150	    FinishOnTruncation,
151	    /// A `Finish` was emitted after cancellation (assertion 5).
152	    FinishOnCancel,
153	    /// A `Finish` was emitted after a mid-stream error (assertion 6).
154	    FinishAfterError,
155	    /// An event other than `Usage` followed the first `Err` (assertion 9).
156	    EventAfterError,
157	    /// A `call_id` carried a number of name-bearing deltas other than one, or
158	    /// the name did not match the fixture's declared tool name (assertion 7).
159	    ToolNameNotExactlyOnce {
160	        /// The call whose name emission was wrong.
161	        call_id: String,
162	        /// How many deltas for that `call_id` carried `Some(name)`.
163	        count: usize,
164	    },
165	    /// A `ProviderData` event named a `call_id` for which the stream carried no
166	    /// `ToolCallDelta` (assertion 8).
167	    ProviderDataUnknownCall {
168	        /// The `call_id` that no streamed tool call used.
169	        call_id: String,
170	    },
171	    /// A call's concatenated `args_delta` did not parse as JSON on a stream
172	    /// that carried a `Finish` (assertion 10).
173	    ToolArgsNotJson {
174	        /// The call whose arguments did not parse.
175	        call_id: String,
176	    },
177	    /// The stream did not produce the minimum evidence its scenario requires,
178	    /// so the assertions would have passed vacuously.
179	    InsufficientEvidence(&'static str),
180	    /// The terminal event carried a different `FinishReason` than the
181	    /// subject's fixture declares, so the bytes served are not the ones the
182	    /// scenario describes (spec §7.1).
183	    FinishReasonMismatch {
184	        /// What the subject's `fixture_finish_reason` declared.
185	        expected: FinishReason,
186	        /// What the stream actually emitted.
187	        observed: FinishReason,
188	    },
189	    /// The run order of the reasoning, text and tool channels differs from
190	    /// the order that the subject's fixture declares. This is a check of
191	    /// fidelity to the wire, not of the contract, which lets the channels
192	    /// interleave freely.
193	    ChannelOrderMismatch {
194	        /// What the subject's `fixture_channel_order` declared.
195	        expected: Vec<Channel>,
196	        /// The runs the stream actually emitted.
197	        observed: Vec<Channel>,
198	    },
199	    /// The observed tool calls, in first-seen `call_id` order, differ from
200	    /// the calls that the subject's fixture declares, by name or by parsed
201	    /// arguments. The match is by position, not by `call_id`.
202	    ToolCallsMismatch {
203	        /// What the subject's `fixture_calls` declared, as (name, arguments).
204	        expected: Vec<(String, serde_json::Value)>,
205	        /// The calls the stream actually emitted, as (name, arguments).
206	        observed: Vec<(String, serde_json::Value)>,
207	    },
208	    /// The stream did not terminate within the per-scenario timeout.
209	    Timeout,
210	    /// The subject's `encodes_stop_reason` disagreed with the scenario's own
211	    /// expectation, so its fixture does not match the script it claims.
212	    StopReasonDeclarationMismatch {
213	        /// What the scenario requires.
214	        expected: bool,
215	        /// What the subject declared.
216	        declared: bool,
217	    },
218	}
219	
220	/// Released by the harness once it has observed the gate event, letting the
221	/// server send the remaining chunks.
222	pub struct GateHandle {
223	    /// Signalled by the harness; the server waits on the paired receiver.
224	    /// Named `tx` rather than `release` so it does not shadow the method below.
225	    pub(crate) tx: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>,
226	}
227	
228	impl GateHandle {
229	    /// Let the server send the remaining chunks.
230	    ///
231	    /// Returns whether the server was still parked on this gate. `false` means
232	    /// it had already run its script to the end, so nothing was being withheld
233	    /// — which is how a cancellation scenario silently degrades into an ungated
234	    /// one, and why `assert_conforms` reads this value rather than discarding
235	    /// it.
236	    pub fn release(self) -> bool {
237	        self.tx.send(()).is_ok()
238	    }
239	}
240	
241	/// What a subject did with a scenario.
242	///
243	/// Declining and being uncaptured are first-class outcomes carrying a mandatory
244	/// reason, not an `Option` a caller can silently treat as a skip. Neither is
245	/// served, so no floor or assertion runs for them. The two are not
246	/// interchangeable: [`Outcome::Declined`] must match [`DECLINED`], and
247	/// [`Outcome::Uncaptured`] must match [`UNCAPTURED`].
248	pub enum Outcome {
249	    /// The subject served the scenario.
250	    Served {
251	        /// The stream returned by the subject's `Model::invoke`.
252	        stream: BoxStream<'static, Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
253	        /// Present only for the cancellation scenarios.
254	        gate: Option<GateHandle>,
255	    },
256	    /// The wire shape cannot physically occur for this provider. The reason is
257	    /// printed in the report and must match the pinned decline set.
258	    Declined(&'static str),
259	    /// The wire shape can occur for this provider, and a capture alone would
260	    /// let the subject serve it, but no fixture that meets the provenance rule
261	    /// exists. The reason must match the pinned [`UNCAPTURED`] table.
262	    Uncaptured(&'static str),
263	}
264	
265	/// One provider backend under test.
266	#[async_trait::async_trait]
267	pub trait StreamUnderTest {
268	    /// Stable subject name, e.g. `"openai/chat"`. Used in failure output and to
269	    /// match rows in the pinned decline set.
270	    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
271	
272	    /// Whether this subject's fixture for `scenario` encodes a stop reason.
273	    /// Cross-checked against the scenario's own expectation.
274	    fn encodes_stop_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> bool;
275	
276	    /// The tool name this subject's tool-call fixtures declare.
277	    fn fixture_tool_name(&self) -> &'static str;
278	
279	    /// The `FinishReason` this subject's fixture for `scenario` declares, or
280	    /// `None` for scenarios that must not produce a `Finish` at all.
281	    ///
282	    /// Exactly seven scenarios end with a `Finish`, and the floor checks this
283	    /// value for all seven: `CleanStop`, `ToolCallCleanStop`,
284	    /// `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`, `ReasoningCleanStop`,
285	    /// `ParallelToolCallCleanStop`, `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop`, and
286	    /// `TruncatedAfterStopReason`, where
287	    /// assertion 3 requires the buffered stop reason to be flushed at
288	    /// end-of-stream. Every other scenario must return `None` — a cancelled or
289	    /// errored stream withholds `Finish`, and a truncation with no stop reason
290	    /// observed never had one to emit.
291	    ///
292	    /// The seven differ in one way only: for the six clean stops a missing
293	    /// `Finish` fails the floor, whereas for `TruncatedAfterStopReason` it is
294	    /// `classify`'s `MissingFinish` (the SMA-531 shape). Either way, a `Finish`
295	    /// that *is* emitted must carry what this method declares.
296	    ///
297	    /// Declared per subject rather than inferred suite-side because only the
298	    /// fixture knows what its bytes encode: a checker that assumed
299	    /// `CleanStop` ⇒ `Stop` would silently accept a fixture that had been
300	    /// transcribed with the wrong stop reason.
301	    fn fixture_finish_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<FinishReason>;
302	
303	    /// The run order of the reasoning, text and tool channels in this
304	    /// subject's fixture for `scenario`, read from the capture. `None` means
305	    /// that the subject makes no claim.
306	    ///
307	    /// `ReasoningCleanStop` requires `Some(..)`. For any scenario that returns
308	    /// `Some(..)`, the floor compares the observed runs with it.
309	    fn fixture_channel_order(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<&'static [Channel]>;
310	
311	    /// The tool calls that this subject's fixture for `scenario` carries, in
312	    /// wire order, read from the capture.
313	    ///
314	    /// `ReasoningCleanStop`, `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` and
315	    /// `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` require a non-empty list. Every other
316	    /// scenario returns `&[]`. For a scenario with a non-empty list, the floor reads the declared tool names from it instead
317	    /// of from [`StreamUnderTest::fixture_tool_name`], and it compares the
318	    /// observed calls with it by name and by parsed arguments.
319	    fn fixture_calls(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> &'static [ExpectedCall];
320	
321	    /// Serve `scenario` and return the subject's `Model::invoke` stream.
322	    async fn stream(&self, scenario: Scenario, cancel: CancellationToken) -> Outcome;
323	}
324	
325	/// How long one scenario's drain may run before the suite gives up on it.
326	///
327	/// A subject whose stream never terminates is a real bug this suite should
328	/// catch, and without a bound it would hang `cargo test` rather than fail it.
329	/// Generous on purpose: it is only ever reached on failure, so it costs nothing
330	/// on a green run.
331	const DRAIN_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
332	
333	/// How long a gated stream must stay silent before the harness accepts that the
334	/// server is parked on the gate and fires cancellation.
335	///
336	/// **Why quiescence and not a named gate edge.** The design spec's §6.1 has the
337	/// harness block on a specific event — a `TokenDelta` for `CancelMidGeneration`,
338	/// the `Usage` the fixture places after the stop-reason chunk for
339	/// `CancelAfterStopReason`. That does not survive contact with Anthropic, which
340	/// emits a `Usage` from `message_start` (`anthropic/stream.rs:79`): "cancel on
341	/// the first `Usage`" would fire before any stop reason was buffered, and
342	/// `CancelAfterStopReason` would silently degrade into `CancelMidGeneration` for
343	/// that subject. Silence is subject-independent, and — unlike an event
344	/// predicate — is itself positive evidence that the server is withholding.
345	///
346	/// **What a slow machine does to it.** Firing *late* (the harness task is
347	/// descheduled, so the window elapses later in wall-clock terms) is harmless:
348	/// the server is parked either way and nothing else is in flight. Firing
349	/// *early* is the dangerous direction, and the timer arms twice with different
350	/// stakes:
351	///
352	/// - **Between two events.** Needs two consecutive pre-gate chunks more than
353	///   this far apart, which the server does not produce: `feed` pushes every
354	///   pre-gate chunk into an unbounded channel with no await between them, so
355	///   they reach the socket back-to-back over loopback. If it ever did happen,
356	///   the consequence is a weaker test — cancellation at an earlier truncation
357	///   point — not a red run.
358	/// - **Before the first event**, which is the arming that can actually fail a
359	///   run. It covers connect, request, response head and first chunk, with
360	///   nothing yet consumed. Should *that* window elapse, the token fires having
361	///   collected nothing and the scenario dies on the "no TokenDelta" floor — a
362	///   spurious failure, not a weaker test. Sub-millisecond on loopback, but it
363	///   is the first thing to suspect behind an intermittent cancel-scenario
364	///   failure, ahead of anything in the provider.
365	///
366	/// The `server_was_parked` evidence below is unaffected in every case.
367	const GATE_QUIESCENCE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(400);
368	
369	/// Run every [`Scenario`] against `subject` and panic on the first thing that
370	/// does not hold.
371	///
372	/// Three guards run in order for each served scenario, and each exists because
373	/// of a specific way this suite could go quietly useless:
374	///
375	/// 1. **The stop-reason declaration is cross-checked.** Assertions 3 and 4 are
376	///    conditioned on whether a stop reason was observed, and that cannot be
377	///    inferred from the emitted events — a provider wrongly suppressing
378	///    `Finish` looks identical to one that correctly never saw a stop reason.
379	/// 2. **The positive-evidence floors run before the assertions.** A stream that
380	///    emits nothing satisfies "ends with `Finish`" trivially, so a miswired
381	///    adapter serving the wrong fixture would otherwise pass every assertion by
382	///    producing nothing at all.
383	/// 3. **Then, and only then, the events are classified** by the crate's
384	///    `classify` function.
385	///
386	/// Afterwards the observed declines and uncaptured pairs are compared against
387	/// the pinned [`DECLINED`] and [`UNCAPTURED`] tables in both directions.
388	pub async fn assert_conforms(subject: &impl StreamUnderTest) {
389	    assert_conforms_with(subject, DECLINED, UNCAPTURED).await;
390	}
391	
392	/// [`assert_conforms`] against explicit pinned tables, so the unit tests can
393	/// drive the stale-row direction without a real row.
394	async fn assert_conforms_with(
395	    subject: &impl StreamUnderTest,
396	    pinned_declined: &[(&str, Scenario, &str)],
397	    pinned_uncaptured: &[(&str, Scenario, &str, &str)],
398	) {
399	    let name = subject.name();
400	    let mut declined: Vec<(Scenario, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
401	    let mut uncaptured: Vec<(Scenario, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
402	
403	    for &scenario in Scenario::ALL {
404	        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();
405	        let (stream, gate) = match subject.stream(scenario, cancel.clone()).await {
406	            Outcome::Declined(reason) => {
407	                declined.push((scenario, reason));
408	                continue;
409	            }
410	            Outcome::Uncaptured(reason) => {
411	                uncaptured.push((scenario, reason));
412	                continue;
413	            }
414	            Outcome::Served { stream, gate } => (stream, gate),
415	        };
416	
417	        let declared = subject.encodes_stop_reason(scenario);

3267	    /// `responseId`, and trims `usageMetadata` to two counts.
3268	    fn tool_call_chunk(
3269	        call_id: &str,
3270	        name: &str,
3271	        args: serde_json::Value,
3272	        prompt_tokens: u32,
3273	        candidates_tokens: u32,
3274	    ) -> Vec<u8> {
3275	        frame(json!({
3276	            "candidates": [{
3277	                "content": { "parts": [
3278	                    {
3279	                        "functionCall": { "name": name, "args": args, "id": call_id },
3280	                        "thoughtSignature": THOUGHT_SIGNATURE
3281	                    }
3282	                ] }
3283	            }],
3284	            "usageMetadata": {
3285	                "promptTokenCount": prompt_tokens,
3286	                "candidatesTokenCount": candidates_tokens
3287	            }
3288	        }))
3289	    }

3291	    /// The scripted response for one scenario, or `None` for
3292	    /// `FragmentedToolName`, which this subject declines, or for a scenario
3293	    /// that it has no capture for (uncaptured).
3294	    ///
3295	    /// Returning an `Option` rather than panicking on the declined or
3296	    /// uncaptured scenarios is what lets [`Gemini::encodes_stop_reason`] call this for *every*
3297	    /// scenario and measure the bytes — see `bedrock::script`'s doc for the
3298	    /// same pattern.
3299	    fn script(scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Script> {
3300	        // The two-delta opening every text scenario shares. Both deltas carry
3301	        // `usageMetadata` — see the module doc's "`usageMetadata` appears on
3302	        // every chunk" section for why. Numbers match
3303	        // `multi_chunk_usage_emits_usage_per_chunk`'s two chunks verbatim.
3304	        let opening = || vec![text_delta("Hel", 1, 1), text_delta("lo", 1, 2)];
3305	        // The opening plus one chunk carrying BOTH the stop reason and usage
3306	        // — see the module doc for why those two are never split across two
3307	        // chunks in this subject.
3308	        let through_stop = || {
3309	            let mut chunks = opening();
3310	            chunks.push(stop_chunk("!", "STOP", 1, 3));
3311	            chunks
3312	        };
3313	
3314	        let (chunks, gate_after, ending) = match scenario {
3315	            // Full stream: deltas, then the combined stop-reason/usage chunk,
3316	            // then the `[DONE]` sentinel and a clean end of body. This is the
3317	            // arm that exercises `model.rs`'s `[DONE]` terminal path
3318	            // (`model.rs:155-158`) — see the module doc's two-terminal-arms
3319	            // section.
3320	            Scenario::CleanStop => {
3321	                let mut chunks = through_stop();
3322	                chunks.push(done());
3323	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
3324	            }
3325	            // The stop reason and usage are observed, then the body simply
3326	            // ends — no `[DONE]` anywhere in this script — so the buffered
3327	            // stop reason has to be flushed by the bare-EOF arm
3328	            // (`model.rs:149-152`), the OTHER terminal path. Together with
3329	            // `CleanStop` this is what makes S2 non-vacuous for this subject:
3330	            // each scenario exercises a different arm of `model.rs`'s event
3331	            // loop, not the same one twice.
3332	            Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Clean),
3333	            // The body ends cleanly mid-generation: no `finishReason` chunk
3334	            // ever arrives, so no stop reason is ever observed. The SCRIPT
3335	            // shape (a delta, then EOF, no `finishReason`) matches
3336	            // `truncated_stream_no_finish`'s envelope
3337	            // (`gemini_streaming.rs:67-69`, HAND-AUTHORED) — `opening()`
3338	            // alone.
3339	            Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Clean),
3340	            // Same prefix, but the connection is torn down without a
3341	            // terminating chunk, so the client observes a transport error
3342	            // (`model.rs`'s `Some(Err(e))` arm) rather than an end-of-stream.
3343	            Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Abort),
3344	            // The stop reason and usage are buffered/observed and *then* the
3345	            // body is aborted, so the error path must not flush a `Finish`.
3346	            // If `stop_chunk` were ever dropped from this script by mistake,
3347	            // this scenario's observable events would collapse to exactly
3348	            // `ErrorMidGeneration`'s (`[TokenDelta, Usage, TokenDelta, Usage,
3349	            // Err]`, from `opening()`'s two `usageMetadata`-carrying deltas).
3350	            // As scripted, `stop_chunk("!", ...)` itself carries a non-empty
3351	            // text part alongside its own `usageMetadata`, so it adds one
3352	            // more `TokenDelta`/`Usage` pair before the `Err`, not merely a
3353	            // trailing `Usage`. [`Gemini::encodes_stop_reason`]'s measured
3354	            // scan is what keeps the two distinguishable at the fixture
3355	            // level regardless of which of those it is.
3356	            Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Abort),
3357	            // One content delta goes out, then the server parks holding the
3358	            // second back (`gate_after: Some(1)` pauses *before* the chunk at
3359	            // index 1, per `server.rs`'s `feed` loop) — no `finishReason`
3360	            // chunk anywhere in this script, so no stop reason exists even
3361	            // after the gate releases.
3362	            Scenario::CancelMidGeneration => (opening(), Some(1), Ending::Clean),
3363	            // The stop reason AND its usage are both observed before the gate
3364	            // — [`stop_chunk`] carries both in one event, so this scenario
3365	            // needs no *extra* usage chunk appended for the gate to sit
3366	            // after, the same shape as `anthropic`'s `message_delta`.
3367	            //
3368	            // **This comment is the only guard for this scenario on this
3369	            // subject.** The harness's own "at least one `Usage` observed"
3370	            // floor (`assert_conforms`'s `floor_violation`) is VACUOUS here,
3371	            // the same way it is for `anthropic`: `text_delta` (module doc,
3372	            // "`usageMetadata` appears on every chunk") already emits a
3373	            // `Usage` on the very first chunk of `opening()`, so that floor
3374	            // is satisfied whether or not the gate sits in the right place —
3375	            // even a gate placed before `stop_chunk` would still show a
3376	            // `Usage` from the first `text_delta`, and pass. An earlier draft
3377	            // of this module confined `usageMetadata` to the stop-reason
3378	            // chunk specifically to keep this floor non-vacuous; the live
3379	            // capture (module doc) does not have that shape (its first chunk
3380	            // carries usage too), so it was removed — fidelity over a
3381	            // convenient floor.
3382	            //
3383	            // So the only thing standing between this scenario and silently
3384	            // degrading into `CancelMidGeneration` under another name is
3385	            // this: `gate_after` is a COUNT — `chunks.len()`, not a
3386	            // hand-typed literal — read *after* `through_stop()` has pushed
3387	            // `stop_chunk` onto `chunks`. That parks the server with
3388	            // `stop_chunk` already sent and the body still open, so
3389	            // cancellation truncates the stream strictly after the stop
3390	            // reason was buffered.
3391	            Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason => {
3392	                let chunks = through_stop();
3393	                let gate_after = chunks.len();
3394	                (chunks, Some(gate_after), Ending::Clean)
3395	            }
3396	            // Declined — see the module doc's "why `FragmentedToolName` is
3397	            // declined" section and `Gemini::stream`.
3398	            Scenario::FragmentedToolName => return None,
3399	            // A whole tool call, transcribed from the live capture (module
3400	            // doc, "Live capture"): the name, arguments, id and
3401	            // `thoughtSignature` arrive together in one `functionCall` part
3402	            // alongside `usageMetadata` and no `finishReason` (see
3403	            // [`tool_call_chunk`]'s doc), then a separate chunk carries an
3404	            // empty text part, `finishReason: "STOP"`, and `usageMetadata`
3405	            // again (see [`stop_chunk`]'s doc on its `text: ""` reuse), then
3406	            // the `[DONE]` sentinel — not itself part of the capture, which
3407	            // ended at bare EOF (see [`done`]'s doc).
3408	            Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop => (
3409	                vec![
3410	                    tool_call_chunk(TOOL_CALL_ID, TOOL_NAME, json!({ "city": "Berlin" }), 58, 16),
3411	                    stop_chunk("", "STOP", 58, 16),
3412	                    done(),
3413	                ],
3414	                None,
3415	                Ending::Clean,
3416	            ),
3417	            // Declined — the scenario serves an anthropic thinking block.
3418	            Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => return None,
3419	            // Not served — see the reason in `stream`.
3420	            Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop => return None,
3421	            // Three parallel calls, then the stop reason: all of
3422	            // `parallel_signed.sse`, which is "Capture 1" of the SMA-827
3423	            // design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-827-gemini-
3424	            // thought-signatures-design.md:299`; the file has no provenance
3425	            // header of its own). Streamed against the Developer API on
3426	            // `gemini-3.8-flash`. Chunks 0 to 2 each hold one `functionCall`
3427	            // (`search`, `weather` Paris, `weather` Rome) with a native id;
3428	            // only chunk 0 carries a `thoughtSignature`. Chunk 3 holds an
3429	            // empty text part with `"finishReason": "STOP"`. The body ended at
3430	            // bare EOF, so no `[DONE]` is sent, and the buffered stop reason
3431	            // is flushed by the bare-EOF arm.
3432	            //
3433	            // No edits: the body is the file, byte for byte. The file already
3434	            // holds the placeholder `SIG_A`.
3435	            //
3436	            // The stop chunk writes `"finishReason": "STOP"` with a space, and
3437	            // `FINISH_REASON_MARKERS` accepts that form.
3438	            Scenario::ParallelToolCallCleanStop => (
3439	                PARALLEL_SIGNED.iter().map(|p| captured_frame(p)).collect(),
3440	                None,
3441	                Ending::Clean,
3442	            ),
3443	            // Not served — see the reason in `stream`.
3444	            Scenario::ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop => return None,
3445	        };
3446	
3447	        Some(Script {
3448	            content_type: "text/event-stream",
3449	            chunks,
3450	            gate_after,
3451	            ending,
3452	        })
3453	    }

1	//! Permissive serde types for one LiteLLM Chat Completions SSE chunk.
2	//!
3	//! Every field is `#[serde(default)]` — including `choices`. Measured against
4	//! LiteLLM 1.97.0: the first delta carries an extra `role`, the finish chunk
5	//! has `delta: {}`, and the trailing usage chunk has
6	//! `choices: [{"index":0,"delta":{}}]` with no `finish_reason` at all. A
7	//! backend behind the proxy may omit more than that, and a single missing
8	//! field would otherwise fail the whole chunk. See the SMA-451 design §9.1.

10	use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer};
11	
12	/// Deserialize `T`, treating an explicit JSON `null` the same as an absent
13	/// key: both fall through to `T::default()`.
14	///
15	/// `#[serde(default)]` on a struct only covers a **missing** key — an
16	/// explicit `null` for a non-`Option` field (a `u32`, a `Vec<T>`) has no
17	/// built-in fallback the way `Option<T>` does, so it would otherwise fail
18	/// the whole chunk. Pair with `#[serde(deserialize_with = "null_as_default")]`
19	/// on any such field that a backend has been observed to send as an
20	/// explicit `null` rather than omitting.
21	fn null_as_default<'de, D, T>(deserializer: D) -> Result<T, D::Error>
22	where
23	    D: Deserializer<'de>,
24	    T: Deserialize<'de> + Default,
25	{
26	    Ok(Option::<T>::deserialize(deserializer)?.unwrap_or_default())
27	}

29	/// One `data:` frame of a LiteLLM Chat Completions SSE stream.
30	#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
31	#[serde(default)]
32	pub(crate) struct StreamChunk {
33	    /// Per-response choices. Only the first is read (see the design's
34	    /// single-choice rationale); a proxy configured with `n > 1` returns
35	    /// more, but that is not this crate's use case.
36	    ///
37	    /// `deserialize_with` covers an explicit `"choices": null` — observed
38	    /// alongside the other permissive-shape quirks noted at module level —
39	    /// which `#[serde(default)]` alone would not.
40	    #[serde(deserialize_with = "null_as_default")]
41	    pub(crate) choices: Vec<Choice>,
42	    /// Token-usage snapshot, present only on the trailing usage chunk when
43	    /// `stream_options.include_usage` is set.
44	    pub(crate) usage: Option<Usage>,
45	    /// Defensive: a backend failing mid-generation can emit an error frame
46	    /// instead of (or alongside) a normal delta. Several OpenAI-compatible
47	    /// backends emit `"error": null` on an otherwise healthy chunk — serde's
48	    /// standard `null` → `None` mapping for `Option<T>` already treats that
49	    /// the same as an absent key, so only a non-null value here is a real
50	    /// error. Unverified against LiteLLM itself: every reproducible failure
51	    /// returns non-2xx JSON before the stream opens.
52	    pub(crate) error: Option<serde_json::Value>,
53	}

55	/// One entry of [`StreamChunk::choices`].

57	#[serde(default)]
58	pub(crate) struct Choice {
59	    /// The choice index, when the proxy reports one.

61	    /// The incremental delta for this choice.
62	    pub(crate) delta: Option<Delta>,

74	    /// into this field.

118	    pub(crate) completion_tokens: u32,

146	    /// Pins the invariant `model.rs`'s mid-stream error check relies on:
147	    /// a JSON-null `error` deserializes to `None`, indistinguishable from an
148	    /// absent key — not to `Some(Value::Null)`.
149	    #[test]
150	    fn null_error_field_deserializes_to_none() {
151	        let c: StreamChunk = serde_json::from_str(
152	            r#"{"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"hi"}}],"error":null}"#,
153	        )
154	        .expect("must deserialize");
155	        assert!(c.error.is_none());
156	        assert_eq!(c.choices.len(), 1);
157	    }
158	
159	    #[test]
160	    fn absent_error_field_deserializes_to_none() {
161	        let c: StreamChunk =
162	            serde_json::from_str(r#"{"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"hi"}}]}"#)
163	                .expect("must deserialize");
164	        assert!(c.error.is_none());
165	    }

169	        let c: StreamChunk = serde_json::from_str(
170	            r#"{"choices":[],"error":{"message":"boom","type":"server_error","code":"500"}}"#,
171	        )
172	        .expect("must deserialize");
173	        assert!(c.error.as_ref().is_some_and(|e| !e.is_null()));
174	    }

176	    /// `#[serde(default)]` alone only covers a *missing* key. An explicit
177	    /// JSON `null` for `choices` (a `Vec`) or `prompt_tokens` /
178	    /// `completion_tokens` (both `u32`) has no built-in `null` handling —
179	    /// unlike `Option<T>` fields — and would otherwise fail the whole
180	    /// chunk. Pins that `null_as_default` closes that gap and that the
181	    /// numeric fields fall back to `0`.
182	    #[test]
183	    fn explicit_nulls_on_non_option_fields_still_deserialize() {
184	        let c: StreamChunk = serde_json::from_str(
185	            r#"{"choices":null,"usage":{"prompt_tokens":null,"completion_tokens":null}}"#,
186	        )
187	        .expect("explicit nulls on non-Option fields must still deserialize");
188	        assert!(c.choices.is_empty());
189	        let usage = c.usage.expect("the usage object itself was present");
190	        assert_eq!(usage.prompt_tokens, 0);
191	        assert_eq!(usage.completion_tokens, 0);
192	    }
193	}

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The translator analysis in §5 is correct. All five captured shapes go through the current translators, and the builder does not need to change any translator. Two things must change before work starts. First, the plan would commit a Gemini fixture labelled "Changed: nothing" after git has changed its line endings. Second, §6.3 breaks a unit test in `src/lib.rs` that the spec does not mention. Some provenance and tracking gaps also need short additions.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
- **The Gemini capture uses CRLF line endings, and git will change them to LF** - The raw `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-860/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/fixtures/tool_call_zero_args.sse` contains four `\r` bytes, so its line endings are CRLF. The other four text captures have none. Line 28 of `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-860/.gitattributes` sets `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/fixtures/*.sse text eol=lf`. So `git add` stores LF. §6.1 still says the edits are "Changed nothing". Its premise is also false: "the existing LF rule covers only the anthropic `*.txt` files". Lines 4, 15 and 28 cover the litellm, openai and gemini fixtures too. | Why it matters: The fixture would be labelled CAPTURED with an edit that its header does not record. That is anti-goal 1 and the same class of defect as SMA-585. The §4 SHA-256 (1327 bytes) would also stop matching the committed payload. | Suggested fix: Write "Changed: CRLF line endings normalized to LF by .gitattributes" in the Gemini header. Give a hash recipe that includes the CRLF step, or give both hashes. In the Gemini script arm, list CRLF→LF under "Edits made here", or send `\r\n` framing so that the script matches the capture. Correct the §6.1 premise. Add "Gemini ends each SSE line with CRLF" to the §4 findings.

### MAJOR
- **Removing the five rows makes `a_conforming_subject_passes` fail** (your check 3) - Removing the scenario from `UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS` alone breaks nothing: only `uncaptured_rows_name_only_allow_listed_scenarios` reads that list. Removing the five `UNCAPTURED` rows does break a test. In `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-860/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs`, the mock `Subject::conforming` reports `ZERO_ARG_UNCAPTURED` for `openai/chat`, `anthropic` and `bedrock` (lines 1361-1375; `BEDROCK_UNCAPTURED` at 1347-1351). The mock tests call `assert_conforms` against the real `UNCAPTURED` table. So `a_conforming_subject_passes` (line 1527) fails with "unexpected uncaptured of ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop". Five tests that expect a panic still pass, but their panic message now contains an unrelated problem as well. `an_uncaptured_outcome_for_a_declined_pair_fails` (line 1852) then passes for two separate reasons, so it no longer tests its one case. | Why it matters: §6.3 names only `declines.rs`. A builder who fixes only the red test leaves a weakened test behind. | Suggested fix: Extend §6.3. Remove `ZERO_ARG_UNCAPTURED` from the three `conforming` arms, from `BEDROCK_UNCAPTURED`, and from the overrides at lines 1861 and 2243.
